title: Carlet's Kasami cyclic-additive conjecture
abstract: Proves Carlet's cyclic-additive conjecture for the Kasami power function: over every finite field of characteristic two with cardinality 2^n and every k coprime to n, the normalized derivative image has the exact coefficient triple count 2^(2n-3) for all distinct nonzero slopes. The development combines the Müller--Cohen--Matthews permutation theorem, multiplicative character sums, Fourier inversion, and a Fermat-cubic Frobenius-kernel argument.

informal.KasamiCyclicAdditive.carlet_kasami_cycli: For every finite field K of characteristic two with |K| = 2^n, every k coprime to n, and all distinct nonzero v₁ and v₂ in K, the coefficient triple count of the normalized Kasami derivative image is exactly 2^(2n-3).
In the normalized range 1 ≤ k < n, the same coefficient triple count is 2^(2n-3), assuming characteristic two, |K| = 2^n, coprimality, and distinct nonzero coefficients.
informal.KasamiCyclicAdditive.kasami_half_size: Under the normalized admissibility hypotheses, the image of the Kasami derivative has exactly half as many elements as the field.
